title: pool build makes no paid call unless asked: a fresh --out path asks a model for every eval regex
goal: benchmarks.py pool build to an --out path with no prior regexes prints the paid calls it would make and their dry-run estimate and makes none without --ask, so a worker's local rebuild (ST-keicy7gn, one unplanned Sonnet call of about 0.06 USD) costs nothing by default; the review section of the kb-sprint skill names paid commands as not allowed in the read-only reviewer's brief, so the reviewer makes none (SP-5i4itd2d: one paid call of about 0.055 USD)

gates.question: How does a pool build get leave to ask the model for the eval checks its --out file lacks?
Does the reviewer brief in the kb-sprint review section name the paid commands, or only forbid a paid model call?

notes: Merged from ST-e6v5v4dt at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: the same failure (pool build to a fresh --out asks Sonnet for about 0.06 USD; listed_ask limits only with --redo; second sprint it happened), its review-section brief clause folded into the goal. Premise: pool build to a fresh --out with no prior regexes makes one paid call for 41 eval rows, estimated 0.088 USD (run 2026-10-13 with sonnet_regexes patched, no paid call): reproduces; and the _self pack for 'may the sprint reviewer make paid model calls' is coverage weak. Plan: TK-3ycnarx5 the --ask flag (gate g1 ask-flag), TK-rwghdnt6 the brief clause (gate g2 name-commands). A build into a copy of the committed file asks nothing, since its checks are cached. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 5 of 15, "Benchmark pool rows: answer regexes, stale rows, the gap row, a pool build that asks before paying and a corrected report"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
